paragraphs.title: The Tribal Portions in the North

easy.q: Which tribe received the first portion in the list?

easy.explanation: The order is Asher, Naphtali, and then Manasseh.
easy.q: Which tribe was next to Asher?

easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “by the border of Reuben… a portion for Judah.”
easy.q: Which tribe received a portion after Reuben?

answers: In strips one south of another
medium.explanation: The tribes are listed in east-to-west strips arranged successively from north to south.
medium.q: How were the first seven tribal portions arranged?

answers: The entrance gate of the city
medium.explanation: Each border marks the boundary between one tribal portion and the next.
medium.q: What does “border” mean in the phrase “by the border of Dan”?

answers: Dan, Asher, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim, Reuben, Judah
Judah, Reuben, Ephraim, Manasseh, Naphtali, Asher, Dan
Dan, Naphtali, Asher, Ephraim, Manasseh, Judah, Reuben
medium.explanation: This is the order given in verses 1–7.
medium.q: What is the order from north toward the south?

answers: They extend from the east side unto the west side
They are all south of the border of Gad
challenge.explanation: The verses repeatedly state that each portion extends from the east side unto the west side.
challenge.q: What do the portions from Dan through Judah have in common?

answers: Each tribe received its own allotment
All the tribes shared one portion
challenge.explanation: The passage assigns a distinct portion to each tribe.
challenge.q: What does the repeated wording “a portion” show?

challenge.explanation: Judah appears after Reuben at the end of the first list.
challenge.q: Which tribe is at the southern end of the first group of seven?

paragraphs.title: The Land Contribution, Priests, and Levites

easy.explanation: Verse 8 says, “the sanctuary shall be in the midst of it.”
easy.q: What was in the midst of the offering?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “for them, even for the priests, shall be this holy oblation.”
easy.q: For whom was the holy oblation appointed?

easy.explanation: Verse 13 places the Levites’ possession against the border of the priests.
easy.q: What holding was next to the priests’ area?

answers: They had kept the LORD’s charge
They were from the tribe of Judah
medium.explanation: They had kept the LORD’s charge and had not gone astray.
medium.q: Why did the sons of Zadok receive the holy oblation?

answers: A portion of land set apart for a special purpose
A gate in the city wall
medium.explanation: The oblation is land offered and set apart for holy purposes.
medium.q: In this passage, what is an “oblation”?

answers: Both were defined portions of the land contribution
Both were outside the land of Israel
Both were assigned to the city gates
medium.explanation: Both are described as measured and designated portions within the offering.
medium.q: What did the priests’ and Levites’ areas have in common?

answers: The area was directly connected with holy service
The area was intended only for farming
The area belonged to the tribe of Gad
challenge.explanation: The sanctuary’s position shows that the area had a sacred purpose.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the sanctuary being in the midst of the priests’ area?

answers: The holy land was not to be transferred to others
The land had to be sold every year
The land could be exchanged for another portion
challenge.explanation: The verse forbids selling, exchanging, or giving away the holy land.
challenge.q: What did the command “They shall not sell of it, neither exchange, nor alienate” mean?

answers: The sons of Zadok had not gone astray from keeping the LORD’s charge
The sons of Zadok served the city
The sons of Zadok received the city gates
challenge.explanation: The sons of Zadok are commended for remaining faithful when others went astray.
challenge.q: What distinguished the sons of Zadok from the Levites in these verses?

paragraphs.title: The City, Open Land, and Agricultural Areas

easy.explanation: Verse 15 calls it a place “for the city, for dwelling, and for suburbs.”
easy.q: What was the remaining area appointed for?

easy.explanation: The city area had equal measurements on all four sides.
easy.q: What shape was the city’s measured area?

answers: Food for those who served the city
easy.explanation: Verse 18 says its increase would be “for food unto them that serve the city.”
easy.q: What was the increase from the eastern and western areas used for?

medium.explanation: The produce was appointed as food for the city workers.
medium.q: Why were the agricultural areas provided for those who served the city?

medium.explanation: The suburbs were measured areas surrounding the city on its four sides.
medium.q: What does “suburbs” mean in “the suburbs of the city”?

answers: People from all the tribes of Israel
medium.explanation: Verse 19 says they would serve it “out of all the tribes of Israel.”

answers: The city was surrounded by open space
The city was inside the sanctuary
The city touched only the sea border
challenge.explanation: The suburbs are specified toward the north, south, east, and west.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the city having suburbs on all four sides?

answers: It provided them with dwelling space and food
It was reserved only for the priests
It was used only for the city gates
challenge.explanation: The remaining area included the city and dwelling places, while its produce supplied food.
challenge.q: What was the relationship between the remaining land and those who served the city?

answers: Each side measured four thousand five hundred
Only the north side was measured
Each side had a different measurement
challenge.explanation: The same measurement is given for the north, south, east, and west sides.
challenge.q: Which detail supports the fact that the city’s sides were equal?

paragraphs.title: The Prince’s Holding and the Southern Tribal Portions

easy.explanation: Verse 22 says that this land “shall be for the prince.”
easy.q: Who received the land between the borders of Judah and Benjamin?

easy.explanation: After the prince’s portion, the passage says, “Benjamin shall have a portion.”
easy.q: Which tribe appears first in the list of the southern portions?

easy.explanation: The order is Benjamin, Simeon, Issachar, Zebulun, and Gad.

answers: On both sides of the holy oblation and the city possession
medium.explanation: The residue was for the prince on one side and on the other of the holy oblation and city possession.
medium.q: How was the prince’s holding positioned?

answers: A portion of land given to a tribe
medium.explanation: The chapter describes land portions assigned to the tribes of Israel.
medium.q: What does “inheritance” mean in the phrase “for inheritance”?

medium.explanation: This is the order given in verses 23–27.
medium.q: What is the correct order of the five tribes south of the contribution?

answers: The prince had land on both sides of the central contribution
The prince had a portion only in the south
The prince had no defined portion
challenge.explanation: The wording places the prince’s holding on both sides of the holy oblation and city possession.
challenge.q: What does “on the one side and on the other” imply about the prince?

answers: To the southern boundary of the land
To Dan’s border in the north
challenge.explanation: Gad’s southern border reached from Tamar to the waters of strife in Kadesh and toward the great sea.
challenge.q: How far did Gad’s border extend?

answers: The land was divided into ordered portions for the tribes
Every tribe received only one city
challenge.explanation: The chapter carefully lists the portions and borders of the tribes.
challenge.q: What does the list of portions reveal about the structure of the land?

easy.explanation: Each side is described as having “three gates.”
easy.q: How many gates were on each side of the city?

easy.explanation: Verse 31 names the gates of Reuben, Judah, and Levi on the north side.
easy.q: Which gates were on the north side?

easy.explanation: The chapter ends with the name, “The LORD is there.”
easy.q: What was the city called at the end of the chapter?

medium.explanation: Verse 32 names Joseph, Benjamin, and Dan on the east side.
medium.q: Which names were on the east-side gates?

answers: The LORD’s presence in the city
That the city belonged to Dan
That the city stood beside the sea
medium.explanation: The city’s name declares that the LORD is present there.
medium.q: What does “The LORD is there” express?

medium.explanation: Verse 33 names Simeon, Issachar, and Zebulun on the south side.
medium.q: Which tribes were named on the south-side gates?

answers: The city was arranged in a balanced way on every side
Only the north side was important
The city had no surrounding gates
challenge.explanation: Three gates are listed for each of the four sides.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from each side having three gates?

challenge.explanation: Verse 34 names Gad, Asher, and Naphtali on the west side.
challenge.q: Which tribal names were on the west-side gates?

answers: The gates commemorate the tribes of Israel
The gates are named only after the priests
The gates are named according to the city’s measurements
challenge.explanation: The gates are named after the tribes of Israel.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the gate names and the city’s description?
